small_guidance:
- Increase BLOCK_PW (e.g. 64 or 128) and sweep num_warps in {4,8} with num_stages in {2,3} via triton.autotune; current 32×4 leaves the 384/4=96 PW dimension under-tiled and launches 128×64×96×3 = ~2.4M programs which is launch-bound.
- Tile the OC dimension inside the kernel (e.g. process BLOCK_OC=8 output channels per program, sharing the loaded x window across OC) — the inner loop reloads the same input patch IC*KH*KW times for every OC, so amortizing that gather across multiple OC accumulators directly cuts global-memory traffic ~8×.
- Replace the scalar inner static_range over (ic,kh,kw) with an explicit tl.dot of a [BLOCK_OC, IC*KH*KW] weight tile against an [IC*KH*KW, NWCOLS] im2col-gathered input tile so the work goes through tensor cores rather than fp32 FMAs.
large_guidance:
- Restructure as an implicit-im2col GEMM where one program computes a tile of (BLOCK_OC × BLOCK_P) pooled outputs: K = IC*KH*KW = 72, M = OC = 64, N = pooled spatial. Use tl.dot over BLOCK_K=72 (padded to 128), accumulate POOL*POOL conv outputs into one pooled value in registers, then sigmoid+sum across (OC, pooled) and atomic-add into out[n]. This converts the kernel from an FMA-bound scalar loop into a tensor-core GEMM with the AvgPool/Sigmoid/Sum fused as the epilogue.
- Switch input layout to NHWC (channels_last) so the K dimension (IC) is contiguous and the im2col gather coalesces; pre-permute x once in forward. Weight should be packed as (OC, KH*KW*IC).
- Make the kernel persistent over the (OC, P) grid per batch element and have it directly produce a per-(n) reduction in shared memory / via cross-warp reduction before a single atomic_add per program — avoiding the current ~2.4M atomics into out[n].
